description: Whole document open in Compose — the input contract for playbook actions operating on the FULL document rather than a selection (compose-summarize; R2: compose-summarize-word-changes for return-from-Word change summaries; future document-wide risk scan / compare). GOTCHA: this scope carries IDENTIFIERS ONLY — no document text crosses the BFF<>UI boundary. The playbook fetches DOCX bytes from SPE server-side via documentSpeId and extracts text itself; do not expect selectionText-style content here (see compose-selection for span-level text). ENRICHMENT: the fetched text arrives with a Semantic Appendix appended (defined terms, cross-references, structural metadata — SemanticAppendixGenerator, FR-22) to reduce hallucination, and any existing track-changes render inline as CriticMarkup ({++insertion++} / {--deletion--} / {>>comment<<}) for READ-IN only. GOTCHA: you (the model) must NEVER emit CriticMarkup back — all edits are written as the structured edit payload (target_text/new_text/rationale) on the compose-selection write path, never as inline markup mutations to this scope's payload. RECOVERY PATH: if documentVersionEtag does not match the document's current SPE etag, the document changed since dispatch was initiated — proceed with an explicit staleness caveat in your output rather than silently treating fetched content as current. EXAMPLE: compose-summarize-word-changes dispatches with documentSpeId + sessionId + tenantId; the playbook fetches the returned-from-Word DOCX, reads its CriticMarkup for prior changes, and emits { summary, changes: [...] } — never a modified DOCX or a markup string.

fields.name: documentSpeId
fields.description: SharePoint Embedded drive-item id of the open document. The session<>document binding key. Always present (Compose binding rule: every document is in SPE). The BFF dispatch endpoint fetches the DOCX bytes from SPE and extracts text server-side for playbook consumption; only the SPE id crosses the BFF<>UI boundary on this scope. GOTCHA: a lookup failure (404) means the document was deleted or moved after the session opened it — surface that as a distinct 'document unavailable' error, not a generic dispatch failure.

fields.name: documentVersionEtag
fields.description: SPE driveItem etag at the moment of dispatch. Lets the playbook detect that the document changed mid-flight and reject stale invocations. Optional; if absent the playbook proceeds without staleness verification. RECOVERY PATH: on mismatch, do not discard the fetch — complete the analysis but flag it as based on a possibly-superseded version.

fields.name: documentRecordId
fields.description: sprk_document GUID when the document has been promoted (post-first-Save). Null for ephemeral pre-Save docs (Path B). When present, enables matter-binding lookups + audit trail joins + the normal Document AI Search indexing pipeline.

fields.name: matterId
fields.description: sprk_matter GUID when the document is matter-bound. Null when the document is unbound or pre-Save. When present, enables matter-scoped knowledge retrieval and writes derived insights to the matter's knowledge graph. GOTCHA: absence does not mean 'no matter' permanently — an ephemeral pre-Save document can be promoted mid-session; do not cache a null matterId as a durable fact across dispatches.

fields.name: documentName
fields.description: Display name of the document (typically the SPE driveItem name). Used by the playbook for UI rendering and citation envelopes. Not the source of truth for identity — that's documentSpeId. GOTCHA: do not use documentName for de-duplication or lookup logic; two distinct documents can share the same display name.

fields.name: documentMimeType
fields.description: MIME type of the document (typically 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document' for DOCX). Carried into RoutingContext.MimeType for content-aware routing (e.g., a future 'summarize-pdf' variant routes off this). GOTCHA: an unrecognized or absent MIME type should route to the default DOCX-oriented handling, not fail the dispatch.

fields.name: sessionId
fields.description: ChatSession id (Redis/Cosmos/Dataverse three-tier persistence key). The playbook writes its summary output as a structured ChatMessage so prior-session continuity (Compose 'prior sessions for this document' UX) preserves the artifact. RECOVERY PATH: if the session cannot be resolved (expired/evicted from the Redis tier), fall back to returning the result without the continuity write rather than failing the whole dispatch.

fields.name: tenantId
fields.description: Azure AD tenant GUID. ADR-015 Tier 3 isolation key; inherited from PlaybookInvocationContext.TenantId. GOTCHA: never use this value to construct cross-tenant queries — every knowledge/precedent lookup this scope enables MUST be scoped to this tenant.

inputs.rationale: The scope carries identifiers + names only — no document text. The playbook fetches DOCX bytes from SPE itself; this keeps the scope payload tiny and avoids re-marshalling the document text through the BFF<>UI boundary on every dispatch.

outputs.expected: Playbook-shape: terminal-node text + structured fields per the invoked action's JPS output schema. For compose-summarize (R1 smoke test target), the Document Summary playbook (id 47686eb1-9916-f111-8343-7c1e520aa4df) is expected to produce the existing PB-002 Document Profile output shape: { summary, keyParties, dates, obligations, riskFlags, confidence } per file-summary.json precedent.

datagovernance.note: Document TEXT is fetched server-side by the playbook; it does not transit the scope payload. The scope itself contains only deterministic identifiers (ADR-015 compliant).
